text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Thursday unofficially rejected the resignation of Transport Minister Alexander Rezes. Rezes was to offically announced his resignation today.

- Meciar re-affirmed that one of Slovakia's main foreign policy priorities was integration to NATO. He said that the country was fulfilling all requirements in the preparation stage of the integration process.

- Meciar said that his ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) would initiate its own referendum to pursue unspecified changes to the constitution, if the contitutional court allows changes to constitution through referendum.

- Jan Carnogursky, leader of the opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said the rulling coalition was preparing a new law on a state of emergency, which will significantly reduce basic human and political rights.
- Steel producer VSZ said it planned to draw an unspecified foreign syndicated loan this year.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Minister of Health Care, Lubos Javorsky, said the ministry will fulfil its promise of a 35 percent pay rise for doctors in 1997, but that this would not happen in the first quarter of the year.

- Slovakia's sole aluminium producer Slovalco said the country's exclusion from integration to western structures would significantly damage its commercial plans and hurt competetiveness. Slovalco exports 90 percent of its production, mainly to EU countries.
- Slovakia's sole shipbuilder, SLK Komarno, said it was developing a new maritime cargo vessel with a load capacity of 8,000 tonnes.
- Russian airline Aeroflot said it would inaugurate a direct route between Bratislava and Moscow.
- Russia will supply Slovakia with six T-154 and IL-86 passenger aircrafts, as part of repayment of its debts to Slovakia. The planes should help create a new Slovak national airline.
- Tyre Producer Matador Puchov said it would invest 790 million crowns this year, of which 200 million should go to development programmes.
